title: Irreducibility of induced modules at Steinberg weights
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], where semisimple and simply connected have the meanings given in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix any split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, the positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, their half-sum character $\rho\in X^*(T)$, and its extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ trivial on the unipotent radical, as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. For every integer $r\ge1$, the rational $S$-module $$E_B(-(p^r-1)\widetilde\rho)=\{f\in F[S]: f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{p^r-1}f(g)\text{ after every commutative }F\text{-algebra extension}\},$$ with left-translation action $(s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$, is simple: it is nonzero and its only linear subspaces stable under the rational coaction are zero and the whole module. Rational coaction has the meaning in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules].

source.place: Part II, 3.18--3.19: the r-th Steinberg module, induced module of highest weight (p^r-1)rho, is simple. WANTED: this book is not local. Online corroboration read: Alexandre, Positivity, plethysm and hyperbolicity of Siegel varieties in positive characteristic, Definition 2.8 and Proposition 2.9, https://doi.org/10.1112/S0010437X24007607. Convention: with positive roots in Lie(B), E_B(-lambda) has highest weight -w_0 lambda, so the displayed module has highest weight (p^r-1)rho. Published corroboration read in the Cambridge PDF, printed pp.263--264: Definitions 2.4 and 2.8 and Proposition 2.9; the characteristic-two condition rho in X*(T) holds by the cited rho-section-modules statement.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] the roots form a reduced root datum with positive system $\Phi^+$ and simple-root base $\Delta$. By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit], $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$; this is an identity in $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, valid in every characteristic, and $\rho\in X$ by [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Consequently $\langle m\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=m\ge0$, so every $m\rho$ with $m\ge0$ is dominant, and $\langle(p-1)\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=p-1<p$, so $(p-1)\rho$ is $p$-restricted. There is no division by $2$ in $F$.

source.place: 22.17--22.22, printed pp.467--469; elementary assembly with the numerical inputs recorded below.

proof.text: For each $k\ge1$ put $m_k=p^k-1$, $\eta_k=m_k\rho$ and $E_k=E_B(-m_k\widetilde\rho)$. Since $p\ge2$, $m_k\ge1$. By [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], $E_k$ is precisely $W_{m_k}$ and is nonzero finite-dimensional rational, with the specified coaction. By [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line], $E_k^U$ is a line of weight $w_0(-m_k\rho)$. Here $w_0$ carries $\Phi^+$ onto $-\Phi^+$, so it is the unique such element of [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit], which gives $w_0\rho=-\rho$; hence $w_0(-m_k\rho)=m_k\rho$. Hence the weight of $E_k^U$ is $\eta_k$.

source.place: 22.17--22.22, printed pp.467--469; elementary assembly with the numerical inputs recorded below.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-induced-weyl-dimension-formula] with the dominant character $\eta_k$ from step 1. Its actual regular-function space and left action are exactly $E_k$, since the extension of $m_k\rho$ is $m_k\widetilde\rho$. For each positive root, $\eta_k+\rho=p^k\rho$ makes the fraction in that formula equal to $p^k$ in $\mathbf Q$. With $N=|\Phi^+|$, this gives $\dim_F E_k=(p^k)^N=p^{kN}$. These are ordinary integer dimensions; no denominator is inverted in $F$.

source.place: II.5.10--5.12, local text WANTED; explicit specialization of the Weyl dimension formula.

proof.text: For each $k\ge1$, choose a rational submodule $0\ne L_k\subseteq E_k$ with least positive vector-space dimension; such a dimension exists since $E_k$ itself is eligible. A proper nonzero submodule of $L_k$ would have smaller dimension, so $L_k$ is simple. By [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight], $L_k^U$ is a one-dimensional highest-weight line. The inclusion maps it injectively into $E_k^U$, so it equals that line and has weight $\eta_k$ by step 2. Inclusions of subcomodules preserve restricted fixed vectors because tensoring an injective map of vector spaces is injective (extend a basis). Thus the assertion is about rational coactions throughout, not just invariance under $U(F)$.

source.place: 22.17--22.22, printed pp.467--469; elementary assembly with the numerical inputs recorded below.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-restricted-rho-simple-dimension], $\dim_F L_1=p^N$. Induct on $k\ge1$ to show $\dim_F L_k=p^{kN}$. For the induction step apply [lem-sfb-restricted-highest-weight-dimension-product] to the three simple modules $L_1,L_k,L_{k+1}$: their weights are $(p-1)\rho$, $(p^k-1)\rho$, and $(p^{k+1}-1)\rho$, and $\eta_{k+1}=\eta_1+p\eta_k$. Dominance and the restriction on $\eta_1$ were proved in step 1. The resulting equality gives $\dim_F L_{k+1}=p^N p^{kN}=p^{(k+1)N}$, completing the induction.

source.place: II.3.16--3.18, local text WANTED; explicit dimension induction, corroborated online by Williamson section 1.4 and Heidersdorf--Wenzl section 7.5.1.

proof.text: In particular $L_r\subseteq E_r$ has the same finite dimension as $E_r$ by steps 3 and 5. Extend a basis of $L_r$ to a basis of $E_r$; equal dimensions leave no additional basis vectors, so $L_r=E_r$. Since $L_r$ is simple and $E_r\ne0$, the module in the statement is nonzero and every rationally stable subspace is zero or all of $E_r$. If the root system is empty, both dimension products are $1$ and the same argument applies.
